rows: You were about to speak. [To North. / North. Vea, my good lord.
Here comes your uncle. / Hot. Speak of Mortimer!
Heir to the crown? / North. He did; myself did hear it.
Therefore, I say, — / Wor. Peace, cousin, say no more :
Hot. I cry you mercy. / Wor. Those same noble Scots
That are your prisoners, — / Hot. I’Il keep them all;
I’Il keep them, by this hand. / Wor. You start away
Those prisoners you shall keep. / Hot. Nay, I will; that’s flat:
We will stay your leisure. / Hot. I have done, i' faith.
To join with Mortimer, ha? / Wor. And so they shall.
Serv. It is, my lord. / Hot. That roan shall be my throne.
Will this content you, Kate? / Lady. It must of force. IExeunt.
A gross fat man. / Car. As fat as butter.
I have forgot the map. / Glend. No, here it is.
In passion shook. / Glend. Cousin, of many men
Glend. I’Il not have it alter'd. / Hot. Will not you?
Glend. No, nor you shall not. / Hot. Who shall say me nay?
And then to horse immediately. / Mort. With all my heart. IExeunt.
Be more myself. / King. For all the world
But I will beard him. / Hot. Do so, and ’tis well.
Of all our fortunes. / Doug. "Faith, and so we should;
Before not dreamt of. / Hot. You strain too far.
Hot. No harm: what more? / Ver. And further, I have learn’d,
And bid it pass? / Ver. All furnish’d, all in arms;
O that Glendower were come! / Ver. There is more news:
Ver. To thirty thousand. / Hot. Forty let it be:
Hot. We 'll fight with him to-night. / Wor. It may not be.
Doug. You give him then advantage. / Ver. Not a whit.
Ver. So do we. / Hot. His is certain, ours is doubtful.
Ver. Do not, my lord. / Doug. You do not counsel well:
Which of us fears. / Doug. Yea, or to-night. / Ver Content.
Blunt. Tut, I came not to hear this. / Hot. Then to the point.
Hot. And may be so we shall. / Blunt. Pray God you do.
I guess their tenour. / Arch. Like enough you do.

Until I meet the king. / Hot. Up, and away!
